a.xlink:title: First 802.1Q tag; "nested 802.1q" is its own shim in the prose, so exactly one more 802.1Q may follow.
Cisco-internal recirculation tag ("resirc" in the paper [sic]); reached via a placeholder EtherType.
First of the four bounded MPLS labels ("up to 4 MPLS headers"); dispatch mechanism borrowed from the Gibb suite (bos select + payload-nibble header).
Single-key dispatch on protocol - the prose never mentions fragments (unlike the Gibb graphs' (fragOffset, protocol)).
Terminal - the prose lists ARP/RARP among the possible followers but gives them no successors (and no ARP body node, unlike the Gibb graphs).
The nested 802.1Q tag; a third is not in the prose's shim list and falls to the default.
Bottom of stack: "MPLS is followed by Ethernet, IPv4, or IPv6". Nibble 0 is the EoMPLS discriminator here (no control word in this tree, unlike Gibb - see README).
Fourth label: the bound is exhausted, so bos=0 (a fifth label) falls to the default - not a recognized sequence.
The inner Ethernet after MPLS - terminal (the prose gives it no successors of its own).
"GRE can also be followed by IPv4/IPv6" - a full inner IP header, one tunnel level.
The "second IPv4 header" (and GRE's inner IPv4): one tunnel level, so it dispatches L4 only - no further GRE or IP-in-IP.
"an IPv6 extension header which, in turn, is followed by TCP, UDP, ESP or ICMPv6" - one level.
GRE's inner IPv6: L4 only, and no re-entry into the extension-header chain (one-level tunnel reading).
